title: Contextual HyperNetworks for Novel Feature Adaptation
authors: Angus Lamb, Evgeny Saveliev, Yingzhen Li, Sebastian Tschiatschek, Camilla Longden, Simon Woodhead, José Miguel Hernández-Lobato, Richard E. Turner, Pashmina Cameron, Cheng Zhang
abstract_snippet: While deep learning has obtained state-of-the-art results in many applications, the adaptation of neural network architectures to incorporate new output features remains a challenge... we propose the Contextual HyperNetwork (CHN), an auxiliary model which generates parameters for extending the base model to a new feature, by utilizing both existing data as well as any observations and/or metadata associated with the new feature.
what_the_paper_supports: CHN is a hypernetwork that acts as a compiler: given observed values for a new feature + feature metadata, it generates feature-specific decoder head parameters (weights + biases). The CHN uses a set encoder (PointNet-style) to aggregate context observations + the base model's internal representation + metadata embedding → outputs parameters. This is a concrete compile pipeline: context → parameters for a new function. The model is evaluated across 3 domains (recommender systems, healthcare, e-learning) with consistent improvement over MAML, k-NN, and mean-imputing baselines.
what_the_paper_does_not_support: Focus is strictly on parameter prediction for extending decoder heads of a pre-trained P-VAE. No formal specification language (GAP-015). No composition between generated heads (GAP-016 weak). No equivalence checking between feature heads (GAP-017). No versioning of generated heads (GAP-019). No execution trace or validation (GAP-020).
paper_core_claims: Contextual HyperNetwork generates parameters for extending a base model to handle novel output features
Uses both existing data (via base model representation) and new feature context (observed values + metadata) as inputs
Single forward pass at prediction time — orders of magnitude faster than retraining or fine-tuning
Set encoder (PointNet-style) processes variable-size context set into fixed-length context vector
Applied to P-VAE base model; shows consistent improvement across recommender systems, healthcare, and e-learning domains
Outperforms MAML, k-NN head averaging, mean imputing, and train-from-random baselines across all context set sizes

GAP-015.reason: No formal specification language for what each generated feature head computes

GAP-016.reason: CHN generates parameters conditionally — a form of context-conditioned compilation. But no explicit algebraic composition between feature heads

GAP-017.reason: No notion of equivalence or interchangeability between feature heads

GAP-018.reason: Fine-tuning from CHN initialization adapts to new data (Fig 9b); no formal state or effect tracking

GAP-019.reason: Each feature gets an independent decoder head; no explicit versioning or registry mechanism

GAP-020.reason: No formal verification of generated parameter correctness

N2_Representation.reason: Base model's latent representation encodes existing features; metadata embedding encodes feature identity; set encoder aggregates context observations into fixed-length vector

N3_Compiler.reason: STRONG MATCH. CHN is a compiler: context set + metadata → feature-specific parameters (Algorithm 1). Set encoder → context vector → [cm; mn] → feed-forward network → θn. The CHN maps a specification (observations + metadata) to executable parameters. Unlike pFedHN which outputs entire model weights, CHN outputs only the feature-specific head, which is more focused and parameter-efficient.

N4_Artifact.reason: Generated decoder head parameters are per-feature artifacts; no lifecycle management

N5_Interpreter.reason: Base P-VAE model serves as interpreter: takes latent z + generated head params → decodes feature values

N8_ComposerRouter.reason: Each new feature gets its own head — implicit routing by feature identity; no inter-feature composition

N9_VersionedRegistry.reason: Training set features' head parameters form an implicit registry; but no versioning or retrieval mechanism

limitations_and_failure_boundaries: Only tested with P-VAE base model — unclear how well it generalizes to other architectures
Generates only simple decoder head parameters (weights + biases), not arbitrary functions
Retraining CHN needed when base model architecture changes
Performance degrades on temporally-ordered features vs random splits (Fig 6)
No formal guarantee that generated parameters preserve model semantics
Scalability: CHN must be retrained for each new base model
No mechanism for removing or deprecating feature heads
strengths_noted: Set encoder enables variable-size context — elegant handling of few-shot regimes (0 to 32 observations)
Metadata conditioning allows zero-shot parameter prediction (context set size = 0, Table 1 metadata-only)
Three diverse domains show consistent behavior: MovieLens (regression), healthcare (imbalanced binary), e-learning (binary)
CHN initialization → fine-tuning outperforms random initialization → fine-tuning (Fig 9b) — strong evidence for transfer
Theoretical: CHN relates to meta-learning (MAML), hypernetworks, and conditional neural processes within one architecture
Only single forward pass at prediction time — practical for real-time deployment
